x-decisions.shape: leaf, with reasons (§7, the smaller mechanism). Stand 24 is the measured assembly of this screen (sf-record-browser: sf-source, sf-table, sf-pagination, sf-modal, sf-toast; 35/35 scenarios), and the view keeps its interface: collection, current, total, open {id}, deleted {ids}, refresh. It does not become that assembly now: its source part is a stand-in with no real component (sf-source, real: false in the parts catalogue), its confirm part (sf-change-confirm) moves in another branch, and §7.4 would stop the table's events at the frame, which ui-admin listens to on the page today (sf-table-action-intent, onSearchEnd …, vocabulary §9.2). Stand 24 on these real parts places this leaf where it placed the assembly (CC 0: the part tag).
x-decisions.version: 1.0.0 → 1.1.0, a minor while sf-table-tree-intent holds a dated alias (§4.10).
x-decisions.events: open {id} is a cancelable request (vocabulary §5 open): sent when a row's view action is chosen, and the host's record.open follows unless a listener refused it; deleted {ids} is the fact after an applied delete (vocabulary §4). The tree's port intents are announced as tree {intent, payload}, sf-data-view-tree; the old sf-table-tree-intent follows once. answer and state keep their DOM names and details (instance_id stays snake_case until the next major).
x-decisions.re-emit: simai/ui-pro#1 item 3: the view sends none of the table's events as its own; the sf-table-* events a page hears are the inner table's, once each (§8: an element never re-emits a part's event). The converter's apply, save, create, query, template-*, column-settings-*, cell-set and move are the table's and are not declared here.
x-decisions.alias-conflict: sf-data-view-saved-view-intent is not this view's event but a page's request to it (a shared save); it stays listened to and is not renamed. The table's names are the table's (its aliases.json).
x-decisions.carries: a carried field is one the detail holds under that very name (SF.Assembly checks it on every event); the rest is named in x-detail.
x-decisions.own-verb-words: answer, state, tree and files-drop are verbs of this view alone; their words are lang events.<verb>.label.
x-decisions.bulk-actions: a page gives the marked rows' actions on its page row's markup (ui-admin: actions="publish:…|delete:…"); a view placed by an assembly makes its own table and page row (light DOM, where the page's sheets reach them) and takes the actions as the list setting bulk-actions [{id, label}], the label from the assembly's language file (§11.3). Stand 24 on the real parts measured the gap.
x-decisions.values: state is the vocabulary's (populated → ready, no-access → refused); total, selected (the open record) and selection (the table's marked rows) are read-only.
x-decisions.actions: refresh, change-query (concurrency latest: the newest answer wins, by the view's sequence), open-view, save-view, delete-view, apply-under-filter, reset-column-settings, clear-selection and notify answer outcomes (../table/js/manifest-actions.js: the port's {answer, reason, message} is the outcome) and take one object or positional parameters (§4.4). apply-projection, update-record and the tree helpers stay the element's helpers.
x-decisions.persistence: the person's sort and page size are kept in SF.Preferences under preferences-key (or collection); nothing is an assembly key (§7.5).
x-decisions.item-shape: the projection's records are the table's rows {id, revision, …}; page and page-size are numbers (vocabulary 1.1.5).
x-decisions.slot-interface: toolbar, content and pagination take page content as it is; they name no interface (§4.5.1) until a trait exists for them — the x-accepts the converter found are component lists, not interfaces.
x-decisions.host-port: connect-port (setHostPort its alias) hands the port; sf-host-port-request is still sent once per connection to a page that answers it, and is not part of this interface (the runtime hands ports down, §4.9).
x-decisions.listened-names: the view listens to the table's and the page row's names of standard 1.3.8 (sf-table-apply, -select, -save, -refresh, -expand, -load-more, -move, -query, -create; sf-pagination-change, -size-change, -apply, -load-more, -selection-clear, -count, -action-change, -action-for-all-change), not to their dated aliases, so it keeps working after 2026-12-01 and takes each act once. Another page size reads from the first page.
x-decisions.own-parts: a view placed by an assembly (the bare tag, data-sf-instance) makes its sf-table and sf-pagination as light-DOM children in its content and pagination slots, where the page's stylesheets reach them; the fallbacks inside the shadow root are drawn without the table's sheet. A page that writes the documented markup gives them itself and nothing is made.
x-decisions.conflict-total: a filter-wide action whose count moved is a conflict carrying the current total (vocabulary §3.1); the page row shows that total at once.
x-decisions.access-codes: a refusal for access is read in both spellings, access_denied (Larena) and access-denied (ui-admin's reference host, stand 24 U2); the value state is refused then.
x-decisions.lang-ru: the title is «Представление данных» in Russian.
x-decisions.template: the shadow layout is in index.js, the migration form; the rows are sf-table's template; skeleton.html is the static first paint.
x-decisions.css-variables: five public variables: the gap, the drop zone's border, fill and words, the toolbar's gap; they are read with the role tokens as fallbacks.
x-decisions.skeleton: skeleton.html: a toolbar bar, row-cap rows (or the table's page) and a page row of bars, settings only.
x-decisions.source-drift: carried by hand: the estimated total «~N» (ui-pro 71ebff1) is the view's behaviour, not a member.
x-decisions.docs: docs.md, where the folder keeps it.
